entries.title: The Last Lamp
entries.text: At the end of the charted lanes a dying star sits inside five brass gears. Whoever built the Orrery left it unfinished on purpose: a machine that only runs when someone has listened to everything else first.

entries.title: The Choir Relay
entries.text: The Choir is a relay repeating one hymn to nobody. Decoded, it is a list of coordinates dressed up as a verse. Every line ends on the same unresolved note, as if waiting for an answer.

entries.title: The Undertow Pulsar
entries.text: A pulsar that counts. Not seconds: arguments. The Undertow keeps the tally of every dispute between the five civilisations and releases it as a slow tide of noise.

entries.title: The Tally Buoy
entries.text: A buoy that has been tallying freight for longer than the Tallow Combine has existed. It is accurate to the crate. It has never once been asked for its opinion.

entries.title: The Psalm Relay
entries.text: The Synod calls it a psalm; the engineers call it a handshake protocol. They are both right. It asks, in very old language, whether the listener intends to stay.

entries.title: The Ember Call
entries.text: A wreck that still sends. Its last log entry is a recipe for hyper coils and a request not to light the Lamp early.

entries.title: The Beacon Echo
entries.text: An echo of a beacon that is not here. It charts neighbouring systems the way a stranger gives directions: confidently and slightly wrong.

entries.title: Ancient Beacon
entries.text: The beacon predates every lane. It charts the nearest stars for whoever is polite enough to scan it, and has done so for so long that its star-charts show constellations nobody alive has seen.

entries.title: A Poem About Debt
entries.text: The logbook's last page is a poem. 'I carried what I was owed and owed what I carried; the lanes forgave neither.'
